audit.reasoning: Piro (Kiowa-Tanoan) went extinct c. 1900 and its entire record is Bartlett's 1850s ~180-word list, Mooney's unpublished 1897 ~105-word marginalia, one Lord's Prayer in Spanish orthography and place names; Glottolog lists no grammar, phonology or sketch, and Sutton 2014 (held, pp. 5, 210-216) confirms no grammatical sketch is possible and that Harrington 1909 remains the best analysis, with Leap 1971 (classification) the only later publication. The record's deciding quotations from Harrington 1909 and Bartlett & Hodge 1909 are verbatim in the held djvu texts; the only defect is a minor locator slip (Harrington's list of Piro sources is on p. 567, not pp. 564-565). not determinable / domain not stated by the source with grade open-text is the correct and final coding; optionally fix the locator to 'Harrington 1909 p. 567' and, as the compilers suggested, replace the domain_quote (a line from Harrington's Tiwa/Te

sources.note: Or-record (TOC + blurb only): the first book-length linguistic treatment of Tanoan Piro since 1909, with a dedicated 'Linguistic Sketch of Piro' (ch. 10), a reconstituted Piro lexicon (ch. 12) and Tanoan segmental correspondences (ch. 14). Since the whole Piro corpus is Bartlett's 1850s vocabulary, Mooney's marginalia and the 1860 Lord's Prayer in Spanish-based orthography, the sketch's phonology section is the one modern place where a statement on what can (not) be recovered about Piro tone/accent versus the tonal Tanoan sister languages would sit; ch. 14 is titled 'segmental' only.
